data.current_description:
Register a search and a URL. When a listing that matches first appears, it is POSTed to your URL — no polling.

The body is `{"webhook_id", "query", "count", "listings"}`, where each listing uses the same schema as /v1/listings. Every delivery carries `X-Omnia-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC of the raw body>`, keyed with the secret returned once at creation — verify it with a constant-time comparison before trusting the payload.

A new subscription starts from the moment you create it; it does not replay history. Deliveries retry until they succeed, so a 5xx on your side is resent rather than lost, and a URL that fails 10 times in a row is parked. Your URL must be public HTTPS. Limit 10 active webhooks per key.
data.description_suggestion: Register a webhook to receive real-time push notifications when new listings matching a saved search first appear. Provide a search query and a public HTTPS URL. Returns a webhook ID and a one-time secret for HMAC signature verification (store securely). Deliveries include `X-Omnia-Signature` header with SHA256 HMAC of the raw body; verify with constant-time comparison. Subscriptions start immediately and do not replay history. Deliveries retry on failure; URLs that fail 10 times are parked. Limited to 10 active webhooks per key.
data.reasoning: Description is detailed but could be clearer about the request/response contract and side effects. Reorganized to emphasize: what you provide (query + URL), what you get back (webhook ID + secret), how to verify signatures, and important behaviors (no history replay, retry logic, parking after 10 failures). Widening the query does not replay history—position is time-based, not row-based. Re-activating a parked webhook (one that failed 10 times) clears its failure count and resumes deliveries.
